summary: Iteration 15 — Chat Settings (wallpaper + chat lock) + Maintenance backfill. 27/27 pytest cases PASS in /app/backend/tests/test_iteration15_chat_settings_maintenance.py. GET /api/chat/settings returns the full documented shape (default_wallpaper, thread_wallpapers, has_pin, use_biometric, lock_chat_tab, locked_thread_ids, presets). PATCH /api/chat/settings/wallpaper correctly handles default-set/clear_default/per-thread-set/per-thread-clear and rejects unknown presets with 400. The chat-lock lifecycle is fully green: setup (200) → second setup (400) → verify wrong (403) → verify right (200) → change PIN (200) → old PIN now invalid (403) → new PIN works (200) → tab toggle PIN-gated → threads list PIN-gated → disable wipes pin/tab/threads → subsequent verify/change/disable all 400 (with `change` returning 403 because the old-PIN verify path fails first — both surface 'no PIN' state cleanly). Maintenance backfill: 403 for non-admin, 200 with {ok,copied_from_status,admin_defaulted} for super_admin; idempotent on second call (0/0). Regression: /api/chat/threads still 200 (returns {threads:[…]} envelope), /api/admin/broadcasts {audience:'all'} still 201 with recipient_count > 0. EMERGENT_PUSH_KEY 401s in backend logs remain expected with placeholder key.
critical_code_review_comments: routes/chat_settings.py — _verify_pin correctly rejects when pin_hash is None; combined with the explicit `if not pin_hash` 400 guards in verify/disable/threads/tab, the lock surface has no by-passable path. PIN regex ^\d{4,6}$ matches PinBody min/max=4-6 so format validation is consistent across models and route bodies.

routes/chat_settings.py — lock_change uses 403 (old PIN incorrect) even when no PIN is configured. Tested and documented: behaviour is consistent because _verify_pin treats a null hash as 'wrong PIN'. If a 400 (no PIN configured) message would be friendlier, consider adding the same `if not current.get('pin_hash')` 400 guard that verify/disable already have. Non-blocking — current behaviour is safe.

routes/chat_settings.py — Wallpaper.value max_length=4_000_000 is generous (accepts embedded base64). Confirm the chat_settings doc stays within Mongo's 16 MB cap if both default_wallpaper and many thread_wallpapers carry base64 images. Consider rejecting kind='image' values larger than ~250 KB on the server side to keep doc bloat bounded.

routes/maintenance.py — backfill is correctly gated on super_admin via require_admin_role('super_admin') and is idempotent by construction ($exists:false guards). Cleanly logs copied/admin_defaulted counts.
server.py — both new routers are wired with the /api prefix (lines 9019-9020) so URLs match the spec exactly.

The backfill test asserts the SECOND call returns 0/0; the FIRST call may also return 0/0 if a prior iteration ran the backfill — that's still a valid pass (idempotency means the DB is already migrated).
